## Load libraries

```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2) 
library(forcats) #added forcats here
```

## Load data

```{r}
wta <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gruggeri/tennis_wta/master/wta_grand_slam_data.csv")

# keep only the finals to get the tournament winners

finals <- wta %>% 
  filter(round == "F")

# calculate total wins by player

total_wins <- finals %>% 
  group_by(winner_name) %>% 
  summarise(total_wins = n()) %>% 
  arrange(-total_wins) %>% 
  ungroup()

# we reorder the winner_name by total wins

total_wins <- total_wins %>% 
  mutate(winner_name = fct_reorder(winner_name, total_wins)) 
```

## Exercise

How would you colour the bars of a defined colour? 

> To know which aesthetic each geom needs, you can for instance type `?geom_fill` in the console, and press enter. The help page will then open, which will give you all the needed information. In this case, we will use the `fill` aesthetic to fill the bars with color.


Choose one of the next options. Try to look at the code before running it and see if you can find the right answer.

**Option 1**

```{r}
total_wins %>% 
  head(n=20) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = total_wins,
                       y = winner_name,
                       fill = "blue")) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Serena Williams won 23 WTA tournaments",
       subtitle =  "Followed by the legendary Steffi Graf with 22 WTA wins",
       x = "Number of WTA Tournaments Won",
       y = "",
       caption = "source: https://github.com/JeffSackmann") +
  theme_minimal()
```

**Option 2**

```{r}
total_wins %>% 
  head(n=20) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = total_wins,
                       y = winner_name)) +
  geom_col(fill = "blue") +
  labs(title = "Serena Williams won 23 WTA tournaments",
       subtitle =  "Followed by the legendary Steffi Graf with 22 WTA wins",
       x = "Number of WTA Tournaments Won",
       y = "",
       caption = "source: https://github.com/JeffSackmann") +
  theme_minimal()
```


> Why is the second one the correct one?

In the first one, we are mapping the colour to a variable called "blue", and therefore it is not understanding that blue is actually a colour we want to set. 
The first option would work if we wanted to map the colour to the variable `total_wins`, for instance.

```{r}
total_wins %>% 
  head(n=20) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = total_wins,
                       y = winner_name,
                       fill = total_wins)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Serena Williams won 23 WTA tournaments",
       subtitle =  "Followed by the legendary Steffi Graf with 22 WTA wins",
       x = "Number of WTA Tournaments Won",
       y = "",
       caption = "source: https://github.com/JeffSackmann") +
  theme_minimal()
```

In this case, it will create a continuous color scale, that is applied to the color of the bars.

From this little exercise, it is important to understand that when you map the colour to a certain aesthetic, it will create a **colour scale**. If you want to set a colour to all your bars (a `color` or a `fill`), then you need to do it outside the `aes()`, and inside the `geom_*` function.


For instance, as in the following:

```{r}
total_wins %>% 
  head(n=20) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = total_wins,
                       y = winner_name)) + 
  geom_col(fill = "lightblue") + # setting a colour for all the bars
  labs(title = "Serena Williams won 23 WTA tournaments",
       subtitle =  "Followed by the legendary Steffi Graf with 22 WTA wins",
       x = "Number of WTA Tournaments Won",
       y = "",
       caption = "source: https://github.com/JeffSackmann") +
  theme_minimal()
```
